dimensions.reasons: The submitted booth is clearly the intended Canadian Space Agency capsule-themed installation: the red Canada pylon is on the left, the bilingual CSA logo screen occupies the central wall, and a large engineered hatch fills the right side. Group B's final image, csa_capsule_booth_final.png, and Group A wide_front_center.png show the requested floor, ceiling canopy, panel wall, screen, and hatch in the correct overall concept.
issues: The hatch content substantially differs from the target: it presents a simplified three-dimensional display rover against a blue star-dotted backing rather than a convincing porthole view of a lunar surface with a photographic/gritty rover.
The result reads as an isolated open-front display diorama against a black void, rather than as a booth installed within the larger exhibition interior visible in the reference.
Several wall forms are simplified and cleaner than the denser molded sci-fi wall construction in the reference.

dimensions.reasons: The main booth construction is coherent in Group A wide_left_threequarter.png and wide_right_threequarter.png: the floor is a thick platform, the pylon and wall panels meet it, and the canopy is visibly connected to the wall/end structures. The screen, hatch frame, bolts, and panel trims are all visibly attached rather than floating.
issues: In Group A detail_hatch_rover.png, the rover's wheels appear to hover above or ambiguously intersect the inner tray, with detached dark oval marks below them that do not clearly read as contact shadows.
The large shallow canopy has a somewhat stage-set-like cantilever and limited visible structural support beyond the back wall and narrow end slab.

dimensions.reasons: The most important visual identities are strong: detail_pylon_screen.png clearly shows a saturated red pylon with raised white maple/star emblems and readable Canada branding, while the central dark-blue screen is unmistakably a CSA sign. detail_hull_hatch.png shows a recognizable sci-fi hatch with layered framing, bolts, grooves, and small red indicators.
issues: The rover in detail_hatch_rover.png is overly toy-like and blocky compared with the more realistic lunar rover image in the target.
The blue star-field alcove and bright white interior tray do not visually communicate lunar terrain.
The right-side hull is predominantly pale silver/white, rather than the more restrained metallic gray of the reference wall.

dimensions.reasons: The author final image, csa_capsule_booth_final.png, is cleanly rendered with good geometric definition, readable graphics, and a coherent presentation-render aesthetic. Close Group A views retain visible panel relief, bolts, screen framing, and a believable booth shell.
issues: The overall result reads more as a miniature architectural visualization or stylized diorama than a physically installed exhibition booth.
Strong cool-white illumination noticeably washes out the pale wall and hatch faces in csa_capsule_booth_final.png, reducing depth and contrast.
The rover and lunar bay lack the material complexity and ground detail needed for the photographic realism of the reference.

dimensions.reasons: The principal left-to-right arrangement is very faithful in wide_front_center.png and csa_capsule_booth_final.png: red pillar at the left edge, horizontal screen on the central wall, and the large hatch/hull section to the right. The broad open white floor, rear wall, and overhead black ceiling with lights create a clear front-facing visitor zone.
issues: The central open floor is much more expansive and empty than the tightly framed reference installation.
The final presentation is centered and diorama-like rather than matching the reference's closer, more immersive slightly off-front interior viewpoint.

dimensions.reasons: The pylon, screen, hatch, wall, and overhead canopy have internally sensible scale relationships, especially in wide_left_threequarter.png. The pylon reaches the ceiling, the screen is a plausible wall-mounted size, and the hatch is large enough to act as a main booth feature.
issues: Without human-scale elements, the very wide empty platform and shallow booth depth make the construction feel somewhat like a scaled presentation model.
The hatch is more compact and square than the tall vertically segmented porthole feature in the reference.

dimensions.reasons: The lighting scheme is visibly intentional: Group A wide views show the dark ceiling canopy, bright front edge strip, and multiple surface-mounted rectangular floodlights, while detail_pylon_screen.png shows the screen as a self-lit dark display. detail_hull_hatch.png also provides visible brushed linear grain and layered metallic trim on the hatch.
issues: The cool white lighting is overly intense on the white/silver wall areas, causing highlight clipping and making distinct hull finishes harder to read in the author final image.
The pylon appears glossier than the requested satin-lacquer finish.
The floor is legible as matte white, but its extreme brightness provides little material variation or subtle reflected grounding.

dimensions.reasons: All major requested booth components are present and visible: white paneled floor, suspended dark ceiling, edge strips, several floodlights, red branded pillar, central CSA screen, metallic hatch frame, wall seams, stiffener-like panels, rivets, and a rover model. These are clearest across csa_capsule_booth_final.png and the Group A detail images.
issues: The requested lunar-surface reveal is missing; the rover sits in a clean display tray with a stylized starry backing rather than on recognizable lunar ground.
The target's more varied raised wall symbols, vent details, and dense panel treatment are only partly represented.

criteria.criterion: The booth is a coherent human-scale CSA capsule environment with the required three-zone organization, proportions, depth, and circulation logic.
The red pillar is complete in form, branding, side placement, and satin-lacquer finish.
criteria.evidence: The left side in detail_pylon_screen and csa_capsule_booth_final clearly shows a tall red freestanding pillar with large white maple-leaf graphic, multiple white four-point star emblems, and readable 'Canada' branding. Its smooth red surface has restrained edge highlights distinct from the brushed gray hatch metal and white floor.

criteria.criterion: The central display is correctly mounted, branded, self-lit, and visibly produces localized screen glow.
The opposing wall is a complete brushed-matte metallic spacecraft hull system with all specified visible structural-detail classes and reference construction language.
The prominent hatch is an integrated hull opening that reveals a recognizable lunar surface and rover at spatial depth.
criteria.evidence: detail_hull_hatch clearly shows a deeply layered, bolted octagonal hatch integrated into the wall and a recognizable wheeled rover inside it, but the view behind/beneath the rover is a smooth dark star-dotted panel and clean stepped tray with oval pads rather than recognizable dusty, rocky, cratered, or otherwise lunar terrain.

criteria.criterion: The overhead system is a dark suspended ceiling fitted with surface-mounted floodlights and visible edge light strips.
The booth floor is visibly white, spatially continuous beneath the stand, and matte rather than glossy.
criteria.evidence: wide_left_threequarter and csa_capsule_booth_final show a broad white floor platform extending continuously across the booth and foreground. Its panel seams and soft illumination are visible without mirror-like reflections, reading as matte.

criteria.criterion: Native area lighting, screen glow, differentiated materials, and staging combine into a cool high-tech image that preserves hull and hatch clarity.
The active author camera is slightly off-front and its final composition clearly communicates every principal booth zone.
The actual author final image is delivered as an openable high-resolution PNG.
The native Blender project is openable, complete, editable, configured for Cycles, and corresponds to the delivered final PNG.

notes: A clearly recognizable CSA capsule-booth recreation with strong object placement, branding, hatch detailing, and overhead lighting. The main fidelity loss is the hatch interior: it becomes a stylized rover display rather than a convincing lunar porthole scene, while bright lighting and a black-void presentation keep the render from matching the realism and installed-exhibition feel of the reference.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
